where: Section 2, 'Two classes' (paragraph on the plain linear unit), and quiz Q3 is built on the same idea
problem: The chapter says a linear unit trained with MSE is bad because 'its gradient fades when the model is confidently wrong'. That is false. With a linear output the gradient of (ŷ − y)² is 2(ŷ − y), which grows as the error grows; nothing saturates. The gradient-fade argument belongs to sigmoid + MSE (correctly given in Q3), not to linear + MSE. A student will carry away a wrong reason for rejecting linear + MSE.
fix: 'A plain linear unit also handles two classes: train it with MSE and predict class 1 when ŷ > 0.5. It is simple, but the output is unbounded and is not a probability, and MSE keeps pulling on points that are already correctly classified far from the boundary (ŷ = 10 with y = 1 still has gradient 2(10 − 1)), so outliers dominate the fit. Cross-entropy is the usual choice.'
